He played [[college basketball]] for the [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU Tigers]]. ==Early life== Mays grew up in [[Baton Rouge, Louisiana]] and attended the [[Louisiana State University Laboratory School]] (U-High), where he began playing on the varsity basketball team in eighth grade. He dunked for the first time as a freshman.{{cite news |last=Lopez |first=Andrew |title=How LSU guard Skylar Mays turned a tragedy into fuel for his dreams of being selected in the 2020 NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/30299175 |access-date=November 14, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 14, 2020}} He was named first-team All-State in his sophomore and junior seasons as he helped lead the Cubs to back to back state championships. As a junior, he averaged 9.1 points, 8.1 assists and 3.2 rebounds.{{cite web|url=https://www.nola.com/sports/article_213331ba-c915-5dd6-9933-bb89781f2ec2.html|title=LSU point guard spot taking shape with Skylar Mays, Jalyn Patterson|first=Andrew|last=Lopez|website=[[NOLA.com]]|date=October 27, 2016|access-date=December 3, 2019}} Mays transferred to [[Findlay Prep]] in [[Henderson, Nevada]] before his senior year and averaged 10.9 points, 5.3 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 2.7 steals in his only season with the Pilots.{{cite web |last=Thompson |first=Dillon |date=February 22, 2019 |title=Skylar Mays: 4 facts about the LSU men's basketball point guard |url=https://www.theadvertiser.com/story/sports/2019/02/22/skylar-mays-lsu-basketball-tigers-louisiana-state-point-guard/2935059002 |access-date=December 3, 2019 |work=[[The Daily Advertiser (Lafayette, Louisiana)|The Daily Advertiser]]}} Rated a three-star recruit, Mays initially committed to play [[college basketball]] at [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|Louisiana State]] during his sophomore year before re-opening his recruitment to other schools shortly before he transferred to Findlay. Mays eventually re-committed to LSU after considering offers from [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]], [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball|UNLV]], [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]], [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]] and [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]].{{cite web|url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/article_a12aefb9-578d-5910-ab7c-9b0ff4c14a06.html|title=Former U-High basketball star Skylar Mays signs with LSU|first=Sheldon|last=Mickles|work=[[The Advocate (Louisiana)|The Advocate]]|date=November 18, 2015|access-date=December 4, 2019}} ==College career== [[File:Skylar Mays.jpg|thumb|left|upright=.7|Mays with [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]] in 2019]] Mays became the Tigers' starting point guard during his freshman year, averaging 8.3 points, 2.2 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.3 steals over 31 games (25 starts).{{cite web|url=https://www.courant.com/sports/basketball/hc-greater-hartford-pro-am-0730-20170729-story.html|title=Tremont Waters' Game Draws Praise In Pro-Am|first=William|last=Paxton|work=[[Hartford Courant]]|date=July 29, 2017|access-date=December 3, 2019}} As a sophomore, Mays averaged 11.3 points, 4.0 rebounds and 3.0 assists as well as 1.6 steals per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/article_086cdc88-4a96-11e9-859d-6bc0e8debded.html|title=Basketball and books: How LSU guard Skylar Mays, an Academic All-American, is making it all work|first=Sheldon|last=Mickles|work=The Advocate|date=May 19, 2019|access-date=December 3, 2019}} He averaged 13.4 points, 3.3 rebounds 2.1 assists and 1.9 steals per game as a junior and was named second team All-[[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) and the conference's scholar-athlete of the year.{{cite web|url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/article_3718fc62-7cdf-11e9-9ffc-035ede760dd2.html|title=LSU's Skylar Mays says he's not yet ready to make a decision on his basketball future|first=Sheldon|last=Mickles|work=The Advocate|date=May 22, 2019|access-date=December 3, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nola.com/sports/article_40ebb817-49d7-5e32-a856-c665bf23cdee.html|title=LSU basketball trio racks up All-SEC coaches awards|first=Amie|last=Just|work=[[The Times-Picayune]]|date=March 12, 2019|access-date=December 3, 2019}} Mays scored his 1,000th career point on February 26, 2019, against [[2018–19 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]].{{cite web|url=https://www.lsureveille.com/daily/skylar-mays-becomes-st-player-in-lsu-history-to-reach/article_106446f0-3a20-11e9-b517-17a570d95b1e.html|title=Skylar Mays becomes 41st player in LSU history to reach 1000 points|first=Brandon|last=Adam|work=[[The Daily Reveille]]|date=February 26, 2019|access-date=February 9, 2020}} After the season, Mays declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]] but ultimately opted to return to LSU.{{cite news |last=Just |first=Arnie |title=LSU's Skylar Mays, Marlon Taylor withdraw from NBA Draft |url=https://www.nola.com/sports/article_dfbaad19-09a5-5716-a6be-46b4897d2a68.html |access-date=December 3, 2019 |work=[[The Times Picayune]] |date=May 28, 2019}} Mays was named preseason first team All-SEC and to the watchlists for the [[Jerry West Award|Jerry West]] and the [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Player of the Year]] awards.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/lsu/Article/Javonte-Smart-Skylar-Mays-All-SEC-LSU-basketball-team-2019-138051017/|title=Skylar Mays, Javonte Smart land on All-SEC preseason teams|first=Billy|last=Embody|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=November 5, 2019|access-date=December 3, 2019}} He was also named the 45th-best collegiate basketball player going into the 2019–20 season by [[CBS Sports]].{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/ranking-the-top-100-and-1-best-players-in-college-basketball-entering-the-2019-20-season/|title=Ranking the Top 100 2019|access-date=December 3, 2019}} Mays scored a career-high 30 points on November 22, 2019, in an 80–78 loss to [[2019–20 Utah State Aggies men's basketball team|Utah State]].{{cite web|url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/article_798451b2-0d8c-11ea-b769-0398a6ec75c8.html|title=LSU basketball lets 19-point lead slip away in brutal Utah State loss|work=The Advocate|date=November 22, 2019|access-date=January 30, 2020}} Mays tied his career high with 30 points along with eight assists and seven rebounds on February 8, 2020, in a 91–90 overtime loss to [[2019–20 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]].{{cite web|url=https://www.wafb.com/2020/02/08/game-updates-no-lsu-vs-no-auburn/|title=Mays scores career-high 30 in No. 18 LSU OT loss to No. 10 Auburn|website=[[WAFB|WAFB.com]]|date=February 8, 2020|access-date=February 9, 2020}} At the end of the regular season he was again named a first team Academic All-American and was selected as the [[List of Men's Basketball Academic All-America Team Members of the Year|Academic All-American of the Year]] as well as First Team All-SEC and was named the scholar-athlete of the year for a second straight season.{{cite web|url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/article_668ec6f0-6223-11ea-8045-9748bcdf27f5.html|title=LSU's Skylar Mays is chosen Academic All-America of the Year |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/2020/03/16/ncaa-tournament-2020-march-madness-west-baylor-michigan-basketball/5055501002/ |access-date=March 19, 2020 |work=[[Detroit Free Press]] |date=March 16, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Atlanta Hawks (2020–2022)=== On November 18, 2020, Mays was selected with the 50th pick in the [[2020 NBA draft]] by the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|first=CJ|last=Moore|title=Skylar Mays goes to the Atlanta Hawks: Here's what they're getting|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2196816/2020/11/18/skylar-mays-goes-to-the-atlanta-hawks-heres-what-theyre-getting/|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=November 18, 2020|access-date=November 19, 2020}} Mays signed a [[two-way contract]] with the team on November 24, 2020, meaning he would split time between the Hawks and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[College Park Skyhawks]].{{cite web |last=Finberg |first=Annie |date=November 24, 2020 |title=Hawks Sign Onyeka Okongwu, Skylar Mays and Nathan Knight |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-sign-onyeka-okongwu-skylar-mays-and-nathan-knight |access-date=November 25, 2020 |website=NBA.com}} On February 13, Mays scored a career-high 20 points against the [[San Antonio Spurs]], cutting a 45-point deficit to just 11 in the second half. Mays played for the Hawks in the [[2021 NBA summer league]], scoring 13 points in 30 minutes on 4-of-11 shooting at his debut in an 85–83 loss against the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|title=Boston Celtics vs Atlanta Hawks Aug 8, 2021 Box Scores {{!}} NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/game/bos-vs-atl-1522100001/box-score#box-score|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 8, 2021}} On August 26, 2021, Mays signed a second two-way contract with the Hawks.{{cite web|title=Hawks Sign Skylar Mays To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/features/hawks-sign-skylar-mays-two-way-contract|last=Rehmann |first=Arman |website=NBA.com|date=August 26, 2021|access-date=August 28, 2021}} On April 7, 2022, the Hawks converted his previously signed two-way contract into a standard NBA contract.{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Convert Contract of Skylar Mays|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/atlanta-hawks-convert-contract-skylar-mays|website=NBA.com|date=April 7, 2022|access-date=April 7, 2022}} ===Delaware Blue Coats (2022–2023)=== On November 4, 2022, Mays was named to the opening night roster for the [[Delaware Blue Coats]].{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/blue-coats-announce-opening-night-roster/n-5895485|title=Blue Coats Announce Opening Night Roster|website=oursportscentral.com|date=November Blazers (2023–2024)=== On March 30, 2023, Mays signed a 10-day contract with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]{{cite web|title=TRAIL BLAZERS SIGN SKYLAR MAYS TO 10-DAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-skylar-mays-to-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=March 30, 2023|access-date=March 30, 2023}} and on October 1, he signed a [[two-way overtime loss to the Sacramento Kings on November 9 in which Mays scored 18 points and had 11 assists in 37 minutes off the bench{{cite web|title=Kings 121-118 Trail Blazers|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/game/_/gameId/401584798/trail-blazers-kings|website=ESPN.com|date=November 8, 2023|access-date=January 17, 2024}} he started 5 games for the injury depleted Trail Blazers in which he averaged 12 points and 8.2 assists per game.{{cite web|title=Skyler Mays 2023-24 NBA Per Game Splits|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/splits/_/id/4066269/type/nba/year/2024/category/perGame|website=ESPN.com|date=January 17, 2024|access-date=January 17, 2024}} On November 12, he signed a standard contract with Portland.{{cite web|author=porfgomez|title=Trail Blazers Convert Skylar Mays To Standard NBA Contact|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-convert-skylar-mays-to-standard-nba-contact|website=NBA.com|date=November 12, 2023|access-date=November 12, 2023}} On January 6, 2024, he was waived by Portland.{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Waive Skylar Mays and Ish Wainright|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-waive-skylar-mays-and-ish-wainright|website=NBA.com|date=January 6, 2024|access-date=January 7, 2024}} ===Los Angeles / South Bay Lakers 2024|access-date=October 15, 2024}} ===Fenerbahçe Beko (2024–2025)=== On October 18, 2024, Mays signed with [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe Beko]] until the end of the season.{{cite web|title=Skylar Mays Fenerbahçe Beko'da|url=https://www.fenerbahce.org/haberler/basketbol-erkek/2024/10/skylar-mays-fenerbahce-beko-da|website=Fenerbahce.org|date=October 18, 2024|access-date=October 18, 2024|language=Turkish}} On January 31, 2025, Mays was released by the Turkish powerhouse.{{cite web|first=Alessandro|last=Maggi|title=Fenerbahce, Skylar Mays officially part ways|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/fenerbahce-skylar-mays-officially-part-ways/|website=Sportando.basketball|date=January 31, 2025|access-date=January 31, 2025}} ===Iowa Wolves (2025)=== On February 5, 2025, Mays signed with [[Iowa Wolves]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{Cite web|url=https://iowa.gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-acquire-skylar-mays-waive-kok-yat|title=Wolves Acquire Skylar Mays;
